RULE. After swapping a citation, re-read the SENTENCE, not the conclusion: name the exact object the source quantifies over (absolute vs relative; presheaf vs its sheafification) and check it is the object in your statement. If the source proves your conclusion by a shorter route, cite THAT and delete the mechanism sentence -- do not keep a mechanism you cannot source because it happens to have a Lean lemma attached.

Campaign B1 was titled "picSharp is a Zariski sheaf", still open, audit-noted "FALSE without the section" -- consistent with th:cmp, inconsistent with the new claim.
